newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Haider wants 150,000 foreigners out.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Haider wants 150,000 foreigners out.

text.p: Austrian far-right leader Joerg Haider said he wants one third of all foreigners working in Austria to be sent home over the next two years, the current affairs magazine News reported on Thursday.
"The number of foreigners employed here must be cut by one third," the controversial leader of the Freedom Party said in an interview.
This would mean repatriating around 150,000 foreigners to make room for Austrians on the domestic job market.
Austrian unemployment hit 300,000 in January, the highest level since World War Two.
Haider said that foreigners who have lived in Austria for less than three years should be forced to leave the country if they lost their job.
If that did not succeed in cutting the number of foreigners by a third, then job permits should not be extended and those with expired permits should be sent home, he added.
Haider reiterated earlier demands that the state halt this year's planned influx of 17,000 foreigners. He claims the government has overstepped the quota of foreigners in Austria by some 40,000.
Haider has won wide popular support for his anti-foreigner policies. In European Parliament elections last October the Freedom Party soared to an all-time high of nearly 28 percent.
